\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هنوز} (hanuz)}{هنوز (hanuz)}]{\fa{هنوز} (hanuz) — still; (with a negative) not yet}

\label{lesson:FA-C136-hanuz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stick, then the Persian for to spin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هنوز}}
\textbf{\fa{هنوز}} — \emph{hanuz} — \textquotedblleft{}still; (with a negative) not yet\textquotedblright{}. Persian negates a verb with \textbf{\fa{ن}} (\emph{na-}, \emph{ne-}): \textbf{\fa{من} \fa{هنوز} \fa{آماده} \fa{نیستم}} — \emph{man hanuz âmâde nistam} — \textquotedblleft{}I'm not ready yet.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{\fa{نیستم}} is the negative of \textbf{\fa{هستم}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hanuz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hanuz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{hanuz}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to stick, then the Persian for to spin, then say \emph{hanuz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{هنوز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Still; (with a negative) not yet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آیا} (âyâ)}{آیا (âyâ)}]{\fa{آیا} (âyâ) — a word that opens a yes-or-no question}

\label{lesson:FA-C136-aya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to spin, then the Persian for still.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آیا}}
\textbf{\fa{آیا}} — \emph{âyâ} — \textquotedblleft{}a word that opens a yes-or-no question\textquotedblright{}. It turns a statement into a question: \textbf{\fa{آیا} \fa{او} \fa{اینجاست}} — \emph{âyâ u injâst} — \textquotedblleft{}Is he here?\textquotedblright{} In speech the rising voice alone often does the same.

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âyâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{âyâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to spin, then the Persian for still, then say \emph{âyâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آیا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A word that opens a yes-or-no question\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مگر} (magar)}{مگر (magar)}]{\fa{مگر} (magar) — surely ... not?; unless}

\label{lesson:FA-C136-magar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a word that opens a yes-or-no question, then the Persian for at all.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مگر}}
\textbf{\fa{مگر}} — \emph{magar} — \textquotedblleft{}surely ... not?; unless\textquotedblright{}. It asks for a \textquotedblleft{}yes\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\fa{مگر} \fa{خسته} \fa{نیستی}} — \emph{magar khaste nisti} — \textquotedblleft{}Aren't you tired?\textquotedblright{}
